model_annotation: Figure 3(a) presents a line plot illustrating the loss values of various models across different methods, with the x-axis representing the number of training steps and the y-axis showing the loss value on a logarithmic scale. The plot includes several lines, each representing a different model or configuration, including Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=380), StrmLLM (n=256), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, T), and SepLLM (n=256). The x-axis spans from 0 to 10000 steps, with tick marks at intervals of 2000. The y-axis ranges from $10^{-1}$ to $10^{1}$, with tick marks at $10^{-1}$, $10^{0}$, and $10^{1}$. The lines for SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, T), and SepLLM (n=256) are consistently below the lines for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=380), and StrmLLM (n=256), indicating lower loss values. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line starts at a loss of approximately 0.8 and decreases to about 0.3 by 10000 steps. The SepLLM (n=64, T) line starts at a loss of approximately 0.8 and decreases to about 0.4 by 10000 steps. The SepLLM (n=256) line starts at a loss of approximately 0.9 and decreases to about 0.3 by 10000 steps. The Vanilla line starts at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to about 0.4 by 10000 steps. The StrmLLM (n=380) line starts at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to about 0.4 by 10000 steps. The StrmLLM (n=256) line starts at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to about 0.5 by 10000 steps. All lines exhibit a general downward trend, indicating a decrease in loss as the number of training steps increases.
